title: Add SM-S928B (e3q-S928BXXS6DZF2) Snapdragon target
body:
## Summary

Add the SM-S928B (Galaxy S24 Ultra international, `e3q`) target for `S928BXXS6DZF2`, plus a hardware test record.

The SM-S928B shares the same Snapdragon SM8650 SoC and the same `6.1.145-android14` kernel series as the existing `e3q-S928USQS6DZF2` target, so `target.h` is derived from the S928U Snapdragon baseline with only `BUILD_FINGERPRINT` and the variant label changed. `p0_fingerprint.h` is generated from the exact raw SM-S928B `S928BXXS6DZF2` Image.

## Hardware validation (SM-S928B, S928BXXS6DZF2)

| Stage | Result |
| --- | --- |
| slide KASLR leak | OK |
| pipe oracle preparation | OK |
| gate physical write | OK |
| **gate hit** | **OK (`gate hits=1`, reproduced multiple times)** |
| probe physical write | OK |
| probe scan | kernel panic (deterministic) |

The gate hit confirms the Snapdragon S928U baseline is correct for the S928B international variant. This is, as far as I know, the first hardware-validated gate hit for the e3q (S24 Ultra Snapdragon) family.

The remaining probe-stage panic is documented in `docs/SM-S928B-S928BXXS6DZF2.md`. I suspect it is leftover rt-mutex state from the probe slot's second slide trigger (gate slide `pselect ret=2` vs probe slide `ret=1`), and would appreciate any guidance on the e3q probe stage.

Related issue: https://github.com/BuSung-dev/Root-My-Galaxy/issues/429
